_readme: Curated road accessibility for the Trishuli / Bhote Koshi flood corridor: can a vehicle get
through today, as distinct from how badly the road was damaged four weeks ago.
Hand-maintained; nothing writes to this file.  tools/build_road_status.py matches each segment
here against data/hdx/derived/roads_in_flood_extent.geojson and the road features of
data/hdx/derived/ems_road_grading.geojson, and writes data/hdx/derived/road_status.geojson,
which the map draws.  A road feature that matches nothing here stays `damaged` and keeps drawing
red, so this file only ever needs the stretches somebody has reported a change on.
To add a segment, append an object to `segments` with:
id             a short kebab-case slug, unique in this file
name           a human name for the stretch
road           the road it belongs to, in words
ref            the highway reference (H01, NH42) or null
from, to       the two ends, in words
status         restored | under_repair | damaged
restored  = traffic is getting through, at whatever width `lane` says
under_repair = work is under way and it is not through yet
damaged   = cut, with no repair reported.  This is also the default for
every road feature that matches no segment, so a `damaged`
entry is only worth adding when the source names the stretch.
lane           two-lane | one-lane | track | null
status_detail  one paragraph: what was done, by whom, when, and what is still missing
as_of          ISO date the status was last confirmed
source_url     the SitRep or article URL, or null
source_title   the publication and headline, or the SitRep number
confidence     high | medium | low
match_names    OSM `name` values this stretch is known by, used to stop a highway's status
bleeding onto a side road that merely runs near it.  A road feature whose
own name is set and matches none of these is never recoloured by this
segment.  Leave the list empty for a stretch with no reliable name.
waypoints      [[lon, lat], ...] along the stretch, in order.  The build densifies this
polyline and matches road features within 120 m of it, 200 m for trunk and
primary features.  Two to eight points is usually enough; they are the
corridor, not a survey.
A segment that captures no road features still draws, as a wide translucent ribbon under the
roads (feature_kind 'segment'), which is how the hill detour routes appear: they run outside
the flood extent and the Copernicus areas, so there are no road features there to recolour.
Run the build with --check after editing; it reports per-segment capture counts.
sources: NDRRMA Situation Report #18 (English), 19 September 2026 - Roads section
Kathmandu Post, OnlineKhabar, Ratopati, Himalpress, Deccan Herald, 6-19 September 2026
Cross-checked against docs/ALTERNATIVE_ROUTES.md and the corridor entries in data/reports.json
notes: No situation report newer than #18 English / #29 Nepali (19 Sep) was retrievable, so the
fast-moving entries (the Betrawati Bailey bridge, the Trisuli Bazar crossing, the last 0.8 km
of the Bidur-Betrawati section) may already be a day or more stale.
A 24th researched segment, Devighat-Kakani-Ranipauwa-Kathmandu, was left out: it was marked
restored purely because no damage had been reported on it, with no source either way.
Two waypoint corrections were applied against the road geometry; both are described in the
status_detail of the segment concerned.  One further waypoint, the middle of the three on
prithvi-jyamireghat-chaukibhir, could not be checked: the Prithvi Highway between Jyamireghat
and Chaukibhir falls outside both the flood extent and the Copernicus areas, so there is no
geometry there to check it against.
Lane counts for the Bailey and Acrow crossings at Devighat, Betrawati and Syabrubesi are
inferred from typical Bailey-bridge width, not stated in any source.

segments.name: Prithvi Highway: Krishnabhir (Mugling-Malekhu section)
segments.status_detail: Road base collapse at Krishnabhir (~70-300 m) repaired with a hillside bypass track; two-way traffic resumed 06:00, 17 September after weeks of one-lane/closed running.
segments.source_title: NDRRMA Situation Report #18 (English), 19 Sep 2026 - Roads section

segments.name: Prithvi Highway: Jyamireghat - Chaukibhir
segments.status_detail: Traffic interrupted the evening of 17 Sep resumed the morning of 18 Sep; treated as one-lane pending confirmation of full two-way running.
segments.source_title: NDRRMA Situation Report #18 (English), 19 Sep 2026 - Roads section

segments.name: Prithvi Highway: Shital Bazaar (Krishnabhir area)
segments.status_detail: Traffic restricted to one lane; hard-rock blasting underway following completion of clearance procedures and a request for Nepal Army support.
segments.source_title: NDRRMA Situation Report #18 (English), 19 Sep 2026 - Roads section

segments.name: Pasang Lhamu Highway: Galchhi - Devighat (via Ratamate)
segments.status_detail: Hillside cutting at Ratamate (~100 m washed out by river erosion) complete, reopening the section to traffic; Thulokhola debris (2-3 m deposits) cleared and Thulokhola-Kashitar-Devighat also cleared. Waypoint 4 of 5 was moved 1.4 km north onto the road alignment: as given it sat in open hillside with no road within 780 m.
segments.source_title: NDRRMA Situation Report #18 (English), 19 Sep 2026 - Galchhi-Devighat-Dhunge-Trishuli section

segments.name: Devighat: Tadi Khola crossing (Acrow/Bailey bridge)
segments.status_detail: 60 m, 5.5 m wide, 50-tonne Nepal Army Acrow/Bailey bridge over the Tadi Khola, built in 5 days, open to pedestrians 10 Sep and vehicles from 11 Sep; SitRep 18 (19 Sep) confirms it remains in operation. Original Tadi Khola bridges (old/new) stay destroyed.
segments.source_title: NDRRMA Situation Report #18 (English), 19 Sep 2026

segments.name: Pasang Lhamu Highway: Devighat - Battar - Bidur - Trishuli Bazar - Gerkhu
segments.status_detail: Devighat-Dhunge and Dhunge-Trishuli sections clear and operational; SitRep 18: "Traffic is operating from Galchhi through Devighat to Battar, Bidur, Trishuli and Gerkhu."
segments.source_title: NDRRMA Situation Report #18 (English), 19 Sep 2026

segments.name: Kolphu (Kolpu) Bridge, Belkotgadhi
segments.status_detail: Open to one-lane traffic following minor repairs; confirmed still holding as of SitRep 18 (19 Sep).
segments.source_title: NDRRMA Situation Report #18 (English), 19 Sep 2026

segments.name: Trisuli Bazar: old & new road bridges over the Trishuli
segments.status_detail: Both Trisuli Bazar bridges (60 m each) remain washed out. A ~48 m Bailey-bridge design for Trisuli Bazaar was reported complete in early Sep, but no installation-start news has been found as of 19-20 Sep; through-traffic still uses the Galchhi right-bank detour instead of a repaired crossing here.
segments.source_title: Kathmandu Post, India sends three Bailey bridges to restore flood-hit connectivity, 13 Sep 2026

segments.name: Right-bank detour: Galchhi - Trishuli Bridge - Kalleritar - Koshikhola - Pimaltar - Darshantar - Chhatre Khola - Gauribesi - Trisuli Bazar
segments.road: Local road (Galchhi rural municipality, right bank)
segments.status_detail: Operational, connecting right-bank communities across the Trishuli in Nuwakot; maintenance continues. Narrow single-lane, no longer the necessary route for through traffic now that Galchhi-Devighat-Trishuli (left bank) is open, but still maintained as a backup/local link.
segments.source_title: NDRRMA Situation Report #18 (English), 19 Sep 2026 (route 6, Trishuli River Right Bank)

segments.name: Pasang Lhamu Highway: Bidur - Betrawati
segments.status_detail: Of the 10 km section, 9.2 km is clear; the remaining 0.8 km (incl. 0.5 km through hard rock) was completely washed away. Road formation and graveling continue, with blasting being coordinated with the Nepal Army; landslides and waterlogged ground keep affecting both the new and existing tracks.
segments.source_title: NDRRMA Situation Report #18 (English), 19 Sep 2026 - Bidur-Betrawati section

segments.name: Bhainse - Betrawati feeder track (bypassing the Bidur-Betrawati gap)
segments.status_detail: About 2.5 km of track opening completed; widening to 6 m and graveling continue along with Hume-pipe and drain installation. Rock cutting continues on the remaining ~300 m between Uttargaya School and Betrawati Bridge; debris (3-4 m deep in places) still being cleared over ~500 m toward Betrawati.
segments.source_title: NDRRMA Situation Report #18 (English), 19 Sep 2026 - Bhainse-Betrawati section

segments.name: Betrawati Bailey bridge (Phalakhu/Falaakhu Khola)
segments.status_detail: Design complete, foundation excavation underway. On 18 Sep, components for a Betrawati Acrow bridge were loaded at the Nepal Army's No. 28 Brigade in Bara, with transport being coordinated with the Department of Roads; a separate 70 m Indian-supplied Bailey span is also en route. Not yet installed as of 19-20 Sep.
segments.source_title: NDRRMA Situation Report #18 (English), 19 Sep 2026 - Bidur-Betrawati / Bhainse-Betrawati sections

segments.name: Dhikure - Phedi Besi Chowk - Hiramunitar - Chogte - Bore Bhanjyang - Sano Khola - Dhanswara - Bhorle - Jibjibe - Bogatitar
segments.status_detail: Reported operational, providing alternative access to Rasuwa while the Trishuli-Betrawati highway section remains damaged; newly operational as of SitRep 14 (15 Sep), maintenance continuing per SitRep 18 (19 Sep).
segments.source_title: NDRRMA Situation Report #18 (English), 19 Sep 2026 - Alternative Routes Connecting Dhading and Rasuwa

segments.name: Kathmandu - Tokha - Chhahare - Gadkhar Bridge - Saramthali - Patikharka - Bogatitar - Kalikasthan - Dhunche
segments.status_detail: Announced by the Ministry of Physical Infrastructure and Transport and reported reopened 28 Aug, two days after the flood; restricted to light four-wheeled vehicles, heavy trucks excluded. Main lifeline into Rasuwa alongside the Dhikure-Jibjibe-Bogatitar route.
segments.source_title: OnlineKhabar, Rasuwa reconnected to road network, 29 Aug 2026 (status carried in SitRep 15, 16 Sep)

segments.name: Devighat bridge bypass: Pipaltar - Pasang Lhamu Highway - Dhamle - Niranjana - Bagkhor - Harre - Deurali - Kolputar
segments.status_detail: Operational, providing an alternative to the (since-repaired) Tadi Khola crossing at Devighat; maintenance continues. Now a backup rather than a necessity since the Devighat Acrow bridge opened.
segments.source_title: NDRRMA Situation Report #18 (English), 19 Sep 2026 - Alternative to Devighat Bridge

segments.name: Pasang Lhamu Highway: Bogatitar - Kalikasthan - Dhunche
segments.status_detail: Open but tightly restricted: OSM way advisory notes read "Only small vehicles (4x4 jeeps) are allowed. Caution due to risk of landslides. Not advised to travel at night. Relief vehicles should register with the police in Kalikasthan before driving to Dhunche." Matches reporting that Bidur-Dhunche is limited to small 4WD vehicles.
segments.source_title: Kathmandu Post, Dhunche has relief supplies; getting aid to villages is the problem, 8 Sep 2026 (via OSM advisory notes, retrieved 17 Sep)

segments.name: Pasang Lhamu Highway: Betrawati - Khalte - Ramche - Kalikasthan (main highway alignment)
segments.status_detail: The direct highway alignment remains cut: Betrawati old and new bridges and the Naya Pul at Khalte are washed out. Traffic instead uses the Dhikure-Jibjibe-Bogatitar and Tokha-Saramthali-Bogatitar bypasses to reach Kalikasthan/Dhunche without using this alignment. No repair-start news found for this direct stretch as of 19-20 Sep. One of the seven waypoints was dropped as out of order; it doubled back past Choktar and lay 1.9 km from any named place.
segments.source_title: Kathmandu Post, 8 Sep 2026; cross-checked against SitRep 18 (19 Sep), no update

segments.name: Pasang Lhamu Highway: Dhunche - Thulo Bharkhu (toward Syabrubesi)
segments.status_detail: "Beyond Dhunche, the road is gone," per a Rasuwa local quoted in the Kathmandu Post; movement past Dhunche is by helicopter/drone only. DoR's plan targets a temporary track by Dashain (mid-Oct) using Bailey bridges over the Bhotekoshi and Chilime, but no construction-start news found as of 19-20 Sep.
segments.source_title: Kathmandu Post, Dhunche has relief supplies; getting aid to villages is the problem, 8 Sep 2026

segments.name: Syafrubesi Bridge (Pasang Lhamu Highway crossing)
segments.status_detail: Part of DoR's Bailey-bridge plan (Syabrubesi needs a ~75 m span); a rope crossing was completed at Syafrubesi for pedestrians/goods (SitRep 15/18). No confirmation the vehicle Bailey bridge itself has been installed as of 19-20 Sep.
segments.source_title: NDRRMA Situation Report #18 (English), 19 Sep 2026 - Suspension Bridges and Rope Crossings

segments.name: Miteri (Nepal-China Friendship) Bridge, Rasuwagadhi
segments.status_detail: Destroyed for the second time (previously rebuilt as a 91 m Bailey bridge after a July 2025 flood, reopened Jan 2026, washed out again 26 Aug 2026 along with its temporary replacement). China has signalled willingness to help rebuild but no formal agreement or rebuild timeline as of 20 Sep; a 5 km stretch of China National Highway 216 toward Rasuwagadhi was also destroyed on the Chinese side.
segments.source_title: Kathmandu Post, Beijing signals support for rebuilding flood-ravaged Rasuwagadhi route, 14 Sep 2026
match_names: 热索临时便桥 रसुवागढीमा अस्थायी मितेरी पुल

segments.name: Pasang Lhamu Highway: Syabrubesi - Timure - Rasuwagadhi
segments.status_detail: The ~16 km Syabrubesi-Rasuwagadhi road (being upgraded under a Chinese-funded project when the flood hit) had large sections swept away along with the border crossing; authorities advise against travel to Rasuwagadhi/Timure. Nepal has asked China to build a temporary track from the border toward Timure and targets a temporary track through to the border by Dashain, but no completion reported as of 20 Sep.
segments.source_title: Kathmandu Post, Beijing signals support for rebuilding flood-ravaged Rasuwagadhi route, 14 Sep 2026

segments.name: Betrawati - Mailung - Haku hydropower access roads
segments.road: Hydropower access roads (Upper Trishuli-1, Trishuli 216, Mailung)
segments.status_detail: Mailung Bailey Bridge, the Upper Trishuli hydropower Bailey bridge, and both Haku (1 and 2) hydropower Bailey bridges remain destroyed with no public repair-start news found in NDRRMA SitReps or web search; these are project access crossings rather than the public highway, and search-and-rescue operations at Upper Trishuli-1 and Chilime were only stood down 19 Sep, suggesting reconstruction has not yet started.
segments.source_title: NDRRMA Situation Report #18 (English), 19 Sep 2026 - Search and rescue section; cf. HDX bridge damage inventory

segments.name: Mid-Hill Highway: Trisuli River bridge near Devighat
segments.status_detail: This separate Mid-Hill Highway crossing of the main Trishuli near Devighat (distinct from the repaired Tadi Khola/Acrow crossing) remains destroyed in the HDX/DoR bridge-damage inventory, with no repair-specific news found; through traffic bypasses it via the Tadi Khola Acrow bridge and the Devighat-Battar-Bidur route instead.
segments.source_title: HDX / HOT flood NPL bridge damage inventory, 6 Sep 2026 (Department of Roads)
